name: Smear
description: Smear (also spelled 'Schmier' or 'Schmear') is a card game played in the northern Midwest of the USA (Minnesota, Wisconsin), closely related to Pitch and High-Low-Jack. It is a trick-taking game typically played with 4 players in partnerships. The objective is to score points for High, Low, Jack, and Game (the 'Smear'), with bids usually starting at 2 or 3. The term 'Smear' also refers to the act of playing a high-point card (like a 10 or Ace) on a partner's winning trick.
deck: Standard 52-card deck (or stripped deck A-10-K-Q-J-9? Usually full deck, but only specific trumps count).

history.origins: Derived from All Fours and Pitch, with a focus on team play and aggressive point-dumping (smearing). The name comes from the German word 'schmieren' (to grease or bribe).
timeline: 1950s: Played in VFW halls and church basements.
history.cultural: A game of subtle signals and bold bids.

setup.players: Four players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other. Some variants use six players in two teams of three or three players without partners.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack; cards in each suit rank A, K, Q, J, 10 down to 2. Some variants use a 54-card pack with one or two jokers as extra trumps, or a stripped 32-card deck (A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7 per suit).
setup.dealing: Deal 6 cards each. Bidding starts left of dealer.

rules.objective: Score points: High (1), Low (1), Jack (1), Game (1). Total 4 points per hand (or more in variants with Joker).
rules.gameplay: Six cards each. One round of bidding (2 to 4); high bidder names trump and leads. Follow suit; may trump when void (in some variants may trump while holding led suit). Four points per hand: High (ace of trump), Low (deuce of trump), Jack (trick with jack of trumps), Game (side with more card points in tricks: A=4 K=3 Q=2 J=1 10=10). First team to reach target (e.g. 15 or 21) wins.
keyRules: Deal 6 cards each; one round of bidding (2 to 4); high bidder names trump and leads.
Must follow suit when possible; may play trump when void.
Four points per hand: High (ace of trump), Low (deuce of trump), Jack (trick with jack of trumps), Game (more card points in tricks).
Bidding side scores what they made if they make bid; else they lose the bid amount. First to target (e.g. 21) wins.

strategy.basic: If you have the Ace and King of Trumps, lead the Ace to draw trumps out, then lead the King to let your partner smear a 10 or Jack. If you are defending, try to save your Low (2) for a trick you can win, or smear it on your partner's trick if you think they are winning.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Game' Count: Counting the 10s is vital. There are four 10s (40 points). Aces are 4 each (16). Kings are 3 each (12). Queens 2 (8). Jacks 1 (4). Total usually around 80 points. Winning the 'Game' point often decides the match.
strategy.advanced: Bidding against the Dealer: The dealer has the last say and can 'steal' the bid for the same amount (in some rules). Bid high enough to force them to 3 or 4.
tips: Don't smear if an opponent might over-trump.
The Jack is worth a game point AND a scoring point.
